chapter: With Chick Webb and Ella Fitzgerald, 1936-39
title: Chick Webb's declining health
summary: Webb's back trouble worsened; fluid was drained and Big Sid Catlett and Bill Beeson subbed on the drums.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Then when we came back to New York -- And this is when we were really getting ready to move up. We came back into New York in the Savoy Ballroom.
This was the year that Chick Webb was really (inaudible), because we were getting ready to go into the Paramount Theater, you know; play the Apollo; our next big thing was the Paramount Theater.
And when -- this hard work begin to tell on Chick. Because every time we close a stage down (Inaudible), the Roseland -- you know, the Roseland

the valet had to and bring him off the stage, (Inaudible) -- go out and pick him up (Inaudible) you know.
Because this was the beginning -- that hump was beginning to tell on him, you know.
What was supposed to have been happening with --
What happened was, that fluid in his back -- I don't know, something was happening with that.
You know, his back was beginning to give him trouble. So they figured they have to have it drained.
So after we closed the Paramount, we went back to the Savoy. But in the meantime, Chick goes to the doctor -- to the hospital here and they operated on that -- they drained it.
The doctor took some fluid out of it or something, you know. And it made him worse.
So then, he brought in Big Sid (Inaudible) -- he used to come up to the Savoy and sit in and play a couple of sets for him -- rest him
